identity: Compared with twelve point, K/X are narrower and L/T wider in 1897; the census confirms K/L. Compared with ten point, U is 13–17% narrower at threshold 205 in 1897, census and document specimens while A is wider. V/W/X and H/N corroborate differences in optical proportions.
visual_review: All 38 visible native crops and final silhouettes reviewed at 185 and 32 pixels, and words at 16/24/40/64/96 pixels including the printed apostrophe. Four final trial sheets, seven threshold sheets, the full native cross-book comparisons and a 36-character comparison with twelve point were inspected. All intended serifs, terminals and bowl joins remain present.
source_choices: Most capitals and figures 0/9 use the census specimen. I/J/R/W and figures 1–8 use the matching 1897 alphabet. I and W avoid the uneven census ink; J retains the complete hook and R the flowing tail. The 1897 figure 8 supplies intact bowl joins missing in the weak census impression. The period is doc8-11; the apostrophe is job8c-07 in MARS’ ELECTRICITY. All four retained books supply selected outlines.
rejected_trials: The initial capital threshold 190 and figure threshold 210 included excess scan fringe. Most capitals now use 175; J/W use 185. Individually reviewed figure thresholds 185/195 retain native completeness with less spread.

Thresholds 175/185 lose the figure 1 beak and figure 2 foot; 175 also loses parts of figures 3/4/5/6/7. Figure 8 needs 195 to retain its lower bowl join, and census 9 needs 185 to close its observed bowl.
The census I has an uneven top serif and W has irregular inner strokes. Matching 1897 impressions provide clearer intact forms; the rejected census outlines remain in the workbench.
geometry: Uniform measured cap scale and rigid source-row rotation. Separate figure groups use locally measured baselines from 1/4/7 at the same physical scale. No independent width fitting, hole filling or drawn replacement strokes.
native_limitations: Minor native print irregularities remain, including the narrow V hairline, J hook and small figure terminals. Optical proportions are preserved without replacing them by idealized outlines.
